items.title: Definition 9.1.2 (2017: 9.1), branched ep⁺-subgroupoids

book.label: §9.1, Definition 9.1.2, p. 402 (2017: Definition 9.1, p. 292)
book.statement: A branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of the ep-groupoid $X$ is a functor $\Theta : X \to \mathbb Q^+$ with (1) $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta) = \{\Theta > 0\}$ contained in $X_\infty$ and $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ paracompact in the topology induced from $|X|$; and, at every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$, (2) an open $U(x)$ and finitely many submanifolds $M_i \subseteq U(x)$ through $x$ with proper inclusions, (3) weights $\sigma_i \in \mathbb Q$, $\sigma_i > 0$, and (4) $\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ for $y \in U(x)$: a local branching structure.

lean.statement: A branched ep⁺-subgroupoid is a functor $\Theta \ge 0$ whose support lies in the smooth set, whose orbit support $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is paracompact, and which at every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ has a local branching structure: an open $U(x)$, finitely many smooth submanifolds $M_i \subseteq U(x)$ through $x$ with proper inclusions, weights $\sigma_i > 0$, and $\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ on $U(x)$. The zero functor and the indicator of a smooth point of $\mathbb R^n$ are examples.

diff: $\Theta$ takes values in $\mathbb Q$ with $\Theta \ge 0$ a field; "the topology induced on $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is paracompact" is a `ParacompactSpace` instance on the subtype; "the inclusion $M_i \to U(x)$ is proper" is `IsProperMap` of the inclusion. The 2017 text's "(ii) and (iii)" in (4) is "(2) and (3)" in 2021 (possible misprint, corrected) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 1).

items.title: Remark 9.1.1 (2017: 9.1) and the last paragraph of Definition 9.1.2, the dimension of a submanifold and $n$-dimensional $\Theta$

book.label: §9.1, Remark 9.1.1, p. 402 (2017: Remark 9.1, p. 291), and Definition 9.1.2, last paragraph, p. 402
book.statement: The dimension of $T_mM$ is locally constant in $m \in M$, the local dimension of $M$. $\Theta$ is $n$-dimensional if at every point of its support the manifolds of a local branching structure can be taken $n$-dimensional (2017: are $n$-dimensional); by a footnote (new in 2021) an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ is not $m$-dimensional for $m \ne n$; $\Theta$ is locally equidimensional if small structures have sheets of one dimension.

lean.statement: A submanifold has dimension $k$ at $a$ if the tangent space of its sub-retract at the chart image of $a$ has dimension $k$; the value does not depend on the data and the chart, is unique, exists at every point, and is invariant under restriction to open sets and under sc-diffeomorphisms. $\Theta$ is $n$-dimensional if at every point of its support some local branching structure has only $n$-dimensional $M_i$; the zero functor is $n$-dimensional for every $n$. The dimensions of the $M_i$ of one structure through $x$ are determined.

diff: The dimension is measured in a chart, since $T_aA$ carries no linear structure (gap G.7). The local constancy of $a \mapsto \dim T_aA$ is not proved in general; it is the hypothesis `HasLocallyConstantDimAt` where it is needed, proved on $\mathbb R^m$ from the trace of $Ds(y)$, and elsewhere the dimensions of the $M_i$ enter as labellings $\mathrm{dim} : I \to \mathbb N$. The footnote ($n$-dimensional $\Theta \ne 0$ is not $m$-dimensional, $m \ne n$) and "locally equidimensional" are not formalized (gap G.93) (Findings, Chapter 9, items 2, 3).

items.title: the restriction of a local branching structure, and Lemma 9.1.7 (2017: 9.2), symmetric structures

book.label: §9.1, Lemma 9.1.7, p. 405 (2017: Lemma 9.2, p. 294), with the restriction remark before it, p. 404
book.statement: A local branching structure on $U(x)$ restricts to $N_i = M_i \cap V(x_0)$ on $V(x_0) \subseteq U(x)$ with the same weights (some $N_i$ may be empty). For every $x$ with $\Theta(x) > 0$ there are an open $U(x)$ with the natural $G_x$-action, properly embedded submanifolds $(M_i)_{i \in I}$, a $G_x$-action on $I$ and weights $\sigma_i > 0$ with (1) $g * M_i = M_{g(i)}$, (2) $\sigma_i = \sigma_{g(i)}$, (3) $\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ on $U(x)$; the proof uses $J = I \times G_x$, $M_{(i,g)} = g * M_i$, $\sigma_{(i,g)} = \sigma_i/|G_x|$.

lean.statement: A local branching structure at $x$ restricts to every open $V \subseteq U(x)$ containing $x$. For a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid and $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ there is, inside every open $V \ni x$, a symmetric local branching structure: the domain of a natural representation $(\Phi, \Gamma)$ of $G_x$, a $G_x$-action on the index set with $\Phi(g)(M_i) = M_{g \cdot i}$ and $\sigma_{g\cdot i} = \sigma_i$, and $\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ there; it is obtained with $J = I \times G_x$, $M_{(i,g)} = \Phi(g)(M_i \cap U)$ and $\sigma_{(i,g)} = \sigma_i / |G_x|$.

items.title: Proposition 9.1.11 (2017: 9.2), the dimensional decomposition

book.label: §9.1, Proposition 9.1.11, pp. 407–408 (2017: Proposition 9.2, p. 297)
book.statement: A branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $\Theta$ determines a unique sequence $\Theta_0, \Theta_1, \ldots$ of branched ep⁺-subgroupoids characterized by (1) $\Theta_k$ is $k$-dimensional and (2) $\Theta = \Theta_0 + \Theta_1 + \cdots$, the sum locally finite. Proof: at $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ take a symmetric structure, split $I = I_0 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup I_n$ by the dimension of the $M_i$ and put $\Theta_k(y) = \sum_{i \in I_k, y \in M_i} \sigma_i$; independence of the structure is Proposition 9.1.12.

lean.statement: For a local branching structure with dimension labelling, $\Theta_k(y) = \sum_{\dim M_i = k,\, y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ is represented on $U(x)$ by the $k$-dimensional structure $(M_i)_{\dim M_i = k}$, $\Theta = \sum_k \Theta_k$ on $U(x)$, and for a symmetric structure $G_x$ preserves dimension and $\Theta_k$ is $G_x$-invariant. The statement of the proposition, "a unique family $(\Theta_k)$ of branched ep⁺-subgroupoids, $\Theta_k$ $k$-dimensional, with $\Theta = \sum_k \Theta_k$ pointwise, and every such family locally finite", is `Proposition_9_1_11`; on the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^2$ it does not hold as we read it: for the indicator $\Theta$ of the $x$-axis $L$, both $\Theta_0 = 1_{\{0\}}$, $\Theta_1 = 1_{L \setminus \{0\}}$ and $\Theta_0 = 0$, $\Theta_1 = 1_L$ are such families. Uniqueness among local decompositions, those given near every point of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ by the dimensional parts of a local branching structure (the form the proof builds): two such decompositions are equal, given Proposition 9.1.12, hence over $\mathbb R^m$ with no hypothesis and under the graph representation in general; in the example, $\Theta_1 = 1_L$ is local and the other decomposition is not. Existence: `dimComponent`, the dimensional part of any labelled local branching structure, is a local dimensional decomposition, the unique one, and locally finite under a dimension bound; `Proposition_9_1_11_local` (Proposition 9.1.11 with "uniquely" among local decompositions, plus local finiteness) holds for every ep-groupoid with object M-polyfold $\mathbb R^m$ (`proposition_9_1_11_local_rn`) and in general under Proposition 9.1.12, the local constancy of dimension and a dimension bound (`proposition_9_1_11_local_of`).

items.title: the category $\mathrm{Gr}(X)$, p. 409

book.statement: There is a well-defined branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $T\Theta : TX \to \mathbb Q^+$, $T\Theta(h) = 0$ for $h \in T_xX$ with $\Theta(x) = 0$ and $T\Theta(h) = \sum_{h \in TM_i} \sigma_i$ over $U(x)$; by the previous discussion it does not depend on the structure, and the local definitions fit together.

lean.statement: Under the independence of V9.13, $T\Theta(h) = \sum_{h \in TM_i} \sigma_i$ for $h$ over $U(x)$, and $0$ over the complement of the support, is well defined, nonnegative and a functor on the tangent ep-groupoid; it is a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of $TX$ if the $TM_i$ are smooth submanifolds of $TX$ (closedness and the paracompactness of $|\mathrm{supp}(T\Theta)|$ for paracompact $|X|$ are proved), and on $\mathbb R^m$ the $TM_i$ are sub-M-polyfolds of $TX$, retracts of $Ts$.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: that the $TM_i$ are smooth submanifolds of $TX$ (the tangent of the sc⁺-retraction is sc⁺ on $TX$), and the paracompactness of $|X|$, neither discussed in the text.
$h \in TM_i$ is read as $h \in T_{p(h)}M_i$; only the zero functor is a witness of the full hypothesis (gap G.99) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 26).

items.title: Lemma 9.2.13 (2017: 9.9), $d_M(x) = 0$ and reduced tangent position

book.label: §9.2, Lemma 9.2.13, p. 419 (2017: Lemma 9.9, p. 307)
book.statement: For a submanifold $M$ of $X$ and $x \in M$, equivalent: (1) $x \in \partial X$ and $d_M(x) = 0$; (2) $T_xM \subseteq T^R_xX$.

lean.statement: For a smooth submanifold $M$ and $x \in M \cap \partial X$: $d_M(x) = 0$ iff $T_xM \subseteq T^R_xX$ (in every chart, the chart image of $T_xM$ lies in the reduced tangent space). For every $x \in M$: $d_M(x) = 0$ iff $T_xM \subseteq T^R_xX$. As printed, with "$x \in \partial X$" in (1), (2) ⇒ (1) does not hold as we read it at a point $p$ of $\mathbb R^n$, which satisfies (2) and lies off $\partial\mathbb R^n$.

diff: Read with $x \in M \cap \partial X$ as the standing assumption, which is where the text uses it, and proved at every $x \in M$ in the form `subDegIndex_eq_zero_iff`. The converse needs a chart of $M$ without boundary near $x$: by the inverse function theorem on $T_xM$ and the step that the projection is injective on $M$ near $x$ ("the image is $M$ near $0$"), which the text does not spell out; the text's complement $Y$ and map $F$ are not needed (Findings, Chapter 9, items 40, 41).

items.title: Remark 9.2.14 (2017: 9.5), $\partial M$

book.label: §9.2, Remark 9.2.14, p. 419 (2017: Remark 9.5, p. 307)
book.statement: $x \in \partial M$ iff $x \in \partial X$ and $T_xM$ is not contained in $T^R_xX$ (2017: in $C_xX$'s reduced part).

lean.statement: $x \in \partial M$ iff $x \in \partial X$ and $T_xM \not\subseteq T^R_xX$; in particular $\partial M \subseteq \partial X$, and $d_M(x) \ge 1$ at such points.

diff: $\partial M$ is the boundary of the induced M-polyfold structure; the text's "not contained in $C_xX$" is equivalent to the reduced-tangent form (`isReducedTangentAt_iff_subset_partialQuadrant`) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 42).

items.title: Proposition 9.2.15 (2017: 9.4), the boundary weights

book.label: §9.2, Proposition 9.2.15, p. 420 (2017: Proposition 9.4, p. 308)
book.statement: For $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \cap \partial X$ and two local branching structures: (1) $\sum_{y \in \partial M_i} \sigma_i$ does not depend on the structure; (2) it vanishes where $d_X(y) = 0$; (3) these sums define a functor $\partial\Theta \ge 0$ supported in $\partial X$.

lean.statement: (1) Under the independence of V9.13, $\sum_{y \in \partial M_i} \sigma_i$ is the same for any two local branching structures whose domains contain $y$. (2) At $y$ with $d_X(y) = 0$ this sum and the corresponding formal sum of tangent spaces vanish, for every structure. (3) $\partial\Theta$, the part of $T_\Theta(y)$ on tangent spaces not contained in $T^R_yX$, is a functor, nonnegative, supported in $\partial X$, and equal to $\sum_{y \in \partial M_i} \sigma_i$ on every structure.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: the independence of Theorem 9.2.1 for (1) and (3).
(1) and (2) need neither $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \cap \partial X$ nor that $\Theta$ be branched, and (2) needs no independence (Findings, Chapter 9, item 43).

items.title: Definition 9.2.16 (2017: 9.7), the boundary $\partial\Theta$

book.label: §9.2, Definition 9.2.16, p. 421 (2017: Definition 9.7, p. 309)
book.statement: In view of the preceding proposition the boundary $\partial\Theta$ of $\Theta$ is the functor uniquely characterized by (1) $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta) \subseteq \partial X$ and (2) $\partial\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in \partial M_i} \sigma_i$ on local branching structures at points of $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$.

lean.statement: $\partial\Theta$ satisfies the text's (1) $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta) \subseteq \partial X$ and (2) the local formula at points of $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$; a functor that vanishes off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ and satisfies (2) at the points of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ equals $\partial\Theta$. As stated, (1) and (2) do not characterize $\partial\Theta$ uniquely as we read them: the zero functor satisfies them for every $\Theta$, and for $\Theta = 1$ on $[0, \infty)$ both $0$ and $\partial\Theta \ne 0$ do.

chips: uniqueness: does not hold as we read it
diff: Hidden hypotheses: the independence of Theorem 9.2.1.

"uniquely characterized" is verified with (2) asked on $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$. "In view of Proposition 9.2.13" before the definition (2017: "Proposition 9.9") is presumably Proposition 9.2.15, and "branched ep⁺-groupoid" is "ep⁺-subgroupoid" (possible misprints) (Findings, Chapter 9, items 44, 45).

items.title: Remark 9.2.17 (2017: 9.6)

book.label: §9.2, Remark 9.2.17, p. 421 (2017: Remark 9.6, p. 310)
book.statement: $\partial\Theta$ has in general no particularly nice properties (the text noted before Lemma 9.2.13 that it is in general not the restriction of $\Theta$ to $\partial X$); "in Section 9.5, Definition 9.3.6" the tame branched ep⁺-subgroupoids are introduced, whose boundaries are nice enough for integration and orientation.

lean.statement: $\partial\Theta \le \Theta$; $\partial\Theta$ is in general not the restriction of $\Theta$ to $\partial X$: for the indicator of the corner $0$ of $[0, \infty)$, $\Theta(0) = 1$ and $\partial\Theta(0) = 0$, while for $\Theta = 1$ on $[0, \infty)$, $\partial\Theta(0) = 1$.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: the independence of Theorem 9.2.1, which the witnesses satisfy.
The forward reference "In Section 9.5, Definition 9.3.6" is to §9.3 (possible misprint, also in 2017) (Findings, Chapter 9, items 45, 46).

items.title: the category $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ and oriented tangent spaces, p. 422

book.label: §9.3, the category $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$, p. 422 (2017 p. 310), and Remark 9.3.1 (2017: Remark 9.7)
book.statement: $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ is defined like $\mathrm{Gr}(X)$ with oriented finite-dimensional subspaces $(L, o)$ of $T_xX$; forgetting orientations is a functor $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X) \to \mathrm{Gr}(X)$ over $X^\infty$. Remark 9.3.1 recalls an earlier notion of orientation.

lean.statement: An oriented tangent space at $y$ is a subset $L \subseteq T_yX$ with a set of positive frames, oriented in a chart and then in every chart; every finite-dimensional tangent space has exactly two orientations; morphisms push oriented tangent spaces forward. $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ is the category of formal sums of oriented tangent spaces over $X^\infty$, with the forgetful functor to $\mathrm{Gr}(X)$ over $X^\infty$.

diff: Frames instead of orientations of vector spaces (gap G.7) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 50).

items.title: Definition 9.3.2 (2017: 9.8), orientations of $\Theta$

book.label: §9.3, Definition 9.3.2, p. 423 (2017: Definition 9.8, p. 311)
book.statement: An orientation of $\Theta$ is a section functor $\hat T_\Theta : X^\infty \to \widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ lifting $T_\Theta$ such that near every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ there is an oriented local branching structure $(M_i, o_i)$, $(\sigma_i)$ with $\hat T_\Theta(y) = \sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i\, T_y(M_i, o_i)$ (9.9).

lean.statement: An orientation of $\Theta$ is a natural assignment $\hat T_\Theta$ of formal sums of oriented tangent spaces at smooth points, lifting $T_\Theta$, which near every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ is $\sum_i \sigma_i\, T_y(M_i, o_i)$ for an oriented local branching structure (continuous orientations $o_i$ of the $M_i$); it defines a section functor of $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$ over $X^\infty$. The zero functor and finite sums of oriented closed submanifolds of $\mathbb R^n$ are oriented.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: the lift condition uses $T_\Theta$, hence the independence of Theorem 9.2.1, discharged on $\mathbb R^m$.
The continuity of $o_i$ is the local constancy of the chart frames (Findings, Chapter 9, item 51).

items.title: Remark 9.3.3 (2017: 9.8), orientations are not unique

book.label: §9.3, Remark 9.3.3, p. 423 (2017: Remark 9.8, p. 311)
book.statement: The local representation (9.9) means exactly that the lift $x \mapsto \hat T_\Theta(x)$ is locally continuous on $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$; an orientable $\Theta$ may have more than two orientations, because of its fractional nature.

lean.statement: The indicator of a point of $\mathbb R^n$ has infinitely many orientations, pairwise distinct, $T_q$ for $q \in (0, 1) \cap \mathbb Q$.

diff: Infinitely many, not only more than one (Findings, Chapter 9, item 52).

items.title: Lemma 9.3.4 (2017: 9.10), orientations are determined by good points

book.label: §9.3, Lemma 9.3.4, p. 423 (2017: Lemma 9.10, p. 311)
book.statement: Two orientations $\hat T^1_\Theta$, $\hat T^2_\Theta$ of a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $\Theta$ which agree at good points are the same.

lean.statement: Two orientations of an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ that agree at the good points agree at every smooth point, under `HasOrientedGoodPointsAt` on the support, which follows from the ball graph representation `HasGraphBallAt` and the level-1 continuity `HasContinuousLevelOneOn`; on $\mathbb R^m$ without hypothesis. Without equidimensionality the lemma does not hold as we read it: for $\Theta = 1_{\mathbb R \times 0} + 1_{(0,0)}$ on $\mathbb R^2$ two orientations agree at all good points and differ at the origin.

chips: mixed dimensions: does not hold as read
diff: Hidden hypotheses: $n$-dimensional $\Theta$; on a general M-polyfold the graph representation and the continuity of frame fields on level 1.

The proof compares the two structures on one family of slices, applying Proposition 9.2.8 to both families together, and compares frames of different sheets by level-1 continuity; the text takes the good-point sequences from the first structure only, a step that needs an argument it does not give (gaps G.97, G.100) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 53).

items.title: Example 9.3.5 (2017: 9.1)

book.label: §9.3, Example 9.3.5, p. 425 (2017: Example 9.1, p. 313)
book.statement: Four smooth $\beta^{\pm\pm}$ with graphs $G^{\pm\pm}$ define $\Theta$ in two ways; orienting by $\pm(1, 0)$ at the origin gives two orientations which coincide at $(0, 0)$ but are otherwise different; there are four possibilities to orient, and the second structure cannot necessarily be oriented to coincide with the first.

lean.statement: For $\beta^{++} = e(s) + e(-s)$ ($e$ = `expNegInvGlue`), $\beta^{--} = -\beta^{++}$ and the two mixed functions, the graphs define a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $\Theta$ of the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^2$ by two structures; the orientations $\hat T^1$, $\hat T^2$ given by $\pm(1, \beta')$ coincide at the origin, differ at $(s, \beta^{++}(s))$ for $s > 0$, and no sign choice for the second structure reproduces $\hat T^1$ near the origin. They also coincide wherever $x < 0$, and the four sign choices of the first structure give four different orientations, none equal to $\hat T^2$.

diff: Hidden hypotheses: none on $\mathbb R^2$.

"otherwise different" and "four different possibilities" do not hold as we read them (at least five orientations with weights $1$); the classification of all orientations of $\Theta$ is not formalized (gap G.101) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 54).

items.title: Definition 9.3.6 (2017: 9.10), tame $\Theta$

book.label: §9.3, Definition 9.3.6, p. 425 (2017: Definition 9.10, p. 314)
book.statement: $\Theta$ is tame if every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ has an open $U(x)$ with the natural $G_x$-action and the properness property and a local branching structure on it whose $M_i$ have equivalent tame structures; in particular every $M_i$ is then a manifold with boundary with corners.

lean.statement: $\Theta$ is tame if at every point of its support there is a local branching structure on a domain with the natural $G_x$-action and the properness property all of whose $M_i$ have a tame induced structure; the zero functor and the indicator of a point of $\mathbb R^n$ are tame.

diff: "an equivalent tame structure" is Part I's tame induced structure (Definition 2.5.18); the consequence "in particular every $M_i$ is a manifold with boundary with corners" is not formalized (gap G.102) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 55).

items.title: Lemma 9.3.7, equal tangent spaces have equal degeneracy

book.label: §9.3, Lemma 9.3.7, p. 426 (new in the 2021 edition)
book.statement: If $Y$ is a tame M-polyfold, $M_1$, $M_2$ submanifolds of the same dimension with tame induced structures and $y \in M_1 \cap M_2$, then $T_yM_1 = T_yM_2$ implies $d_{M_1}(y) = d_{M_2}(y)$.

lean.statement: For submanifolds $M_1$, $M_2$ with tame induced structures and $y \in M_1 \cap M_2$, $T_yM_1 = T_yM_2$ implies $d_{M_1}(y) = d_{M_2}(y)$.

diff: Neither "$Y$ tame" nor "of the same dimension" is needed; in the proof "$T_0O \cap C = T^R_0O$" is read through the linearity of the chart image of $T_0M$ (Findings, Chapter 9, item 56).

items.title: Definition 9.3.8 (2017: 9.9), the boundary orientation of an oriented $M$

book.label: §9.3, Definition 9.3.8, p. 427 (2017: Definition 9.9, p. 313)
book.statement: For an oriented $n$-dimensional $(M, o)$ and $y \in \partial M$ with $d_M(y) = 1$, a basis $(a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1})$ of $T_y\partial M$ is positive iff $(e, a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1})$ is positive for $o_y$, $e$ an outward pointing vector; this orients $\partial M$ near $y$.

lean.statement: For an oriented $(M, o)$, a hyperplane $K$ of $T_yM$ and $e \notin K$, the frames $(a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1})$ of $K$ with $(e, a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1})$ positive orient $K$, and the orientation is unchanged under $e \mapsto ce + k$, $c > 0$, $k \in K$; both orientations occur.

diff: $T_y\partial M$ and the outward vector enter as data $K$, $e$; that $T_y\partial M = T^R_yM$ and the outward half-space are determined by $M$ (through the cones $C_yM$) is not formalized (gap G.103) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 57).

items.title: (9.11) and Proposition 9.3.9, the boundary orientation does not depend on the structure

book.label: §9.3, Proposition 9.3.9, p. 428 (new in the 2021 edition), with (9.11), p. 427
book.statement: For two oriented local branching structures the parts of $\hat T_\Theta(y)$ of each degree $\ell = d_{M_i}(y)$ agree (9.11), since tangent spaces of different degree never coincide (Lemma 9.3.7); the definition of $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}$ does not depend on the structure.

lean.statement: For two oriented local branching structures with tame $M_i$ and the same oriented sum at $y$, the parts of degree $\ell = d_{M_i}(y)$ agree for every $\ell$ (9.11); hence (9.12) gives the same value for every structure, and vanishes at smooth points off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$.

items.title: Definition 9.3.10 (2017: 9.11), the oriented boundary $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}$

book.label: §9.3, Definition 9.3.10, p. 428 (2017: Definition 9.11, p. 314)
book.statement: For an oriented tame $\Theta$, $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}(y) = 0$ off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ and $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}(y) = \sum_{y \in \partial M_i, d_{M_i}(y) = 1} \sigma_i\, T_y(\partial M_i, o_{\partial M_i})$ on $U(x)$ (9.12).

lean.statement: $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}(y) = 0$ off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ and $\sum_{d_{M_i}(y) = 1} \sigma_i\, T_y(\partial M_i, o_{\partial M_i})$ on a structure (9.12).

items.title: Definition 9.4.1 (2017: 9.12), the relative tangent space and essential points

book.label: §9.4, Definition 9.4.1, p. 429 (2017: Definition 9.12, p. 315)
book.statement: For $K \subseteq M$, $M$ a smooth manifold with boundary and corners, $T^K_zM$ is the linear hull of the unit vectors $e = \lim \varphi(z_k)/|\varphi(z_k)|$, $z_k \to z$ in $K \setminus \{z\}$, in a chart centred at $z$, independent of the chart; $z \in K$ is essential if it is a limit of $z_k \in K$ with $T^K_{z_k}M = T_{z_k}M$.

lean.statement: For a subset $K$ of a finite-dimensional manifold with corners, $T^K_zM$ is the span of the limits of unit directions $\varphi(z_k)/|\varphi(z_k)|$, $z_k \to z$ in $K \setminus \{z\}$, in a chart centred at $z$, independent of the chart; $z \in K$ is essential if it is a limit of $z_k \in K$ with $T^K_{z_k}M = T_{z_k}M$. For two crossing lines in $\mathbb R^2$ the essential set is $\{0\}$.

diff: On Mathlib manifolds with corners, the span of Mathlib's tangent cone in a chart (Findings, Chapter 9, item 70).

items.title: Lemma 9.4.2 (2017: 9.11), the essential set is closed

book.label: §9.4, Lemma 9.4.2, p. 430 (2017: Lemma 9.11, p. 315)
book.statement: $K^e$ is closed in $K$, so $K \setminus K^e$ is open in $K$.

lean.statement: $K^e$ is closed in $K$ and $K \setminus K^e$ is open in $K$.

items.title: Property (T) (2017 p. 316)

book.label: §9.4, Property (T), p. 430 (2017 p. 316)
book.statement: (T): if $y_0 \in M_i \cap M_{i'}$, $T_{y_0}M_i = T_{y_0}M_{i'}$ and $o_{i,y_0} = \varepsilon\, o_{i',y_0}$, then $T_y(M_i, o_i) = T_y(M_{i'}, \varepsilon o_{i'})$ for all $y \in M_i \cap M_{i'}$ with $T_yM_i = T_yM_{i'}$. Lemma 9.4.3: (T) holds after restricting to a smaller $U'(x)$.

lean.statement: An oriented local branching structure has Property (T) on $V$ if, whenever two sheets have the same tangent space at a point of $V$ and their orientations there are related by $\varepsilon$, they are related by $\varepsilon$ at every point of $V$ where their tangent spaces agree; the first structure of Example 9.3.5 has it.

diff: Lemma 9.4.3, that (T) holds after shrinking $U(x)$, is not formalized (gap G.104) (Findings, Chapter 9, item 71).

items.title: Lemma 9.4.4 (2017: 9.13), essential in $M_i$ iff essential in $M_{i'}$

book.label: §9.4, Lemma 9.4.4, p. 431 (2017: Lemma 9.13, p. 317)
book.statement: If $z \in K(i, i') = M_i \cap M_{i'}$ is essential for $K(i, i') \subseteq M_i$, it is essential for $K(i, i') \subseteq M_{i'}$; so $K(i, i')^e$, $K(i, i')^{ne}$ do not depend on the reference sheet (proof left to the reader).

chips: mixed dimensions: not as we read it

For M-polyfold sheets, which carry no Mathlib manifold structure, Lemmas 9.4.4 and 9.4.6 are the fields of `SheetGeometry` (gap G.105); the note in Definition 9.4.7 ($i \sim_y i'$ implies $T_yM_i = T_yM_{i'}$) is its field `submanifoldTangent_eq` (Findings, Chapter 9, item 72).

items.title: Definition 9.4.5 (2017: 9.13), sets of measure zero

book.label: §9.4, Definition 9.4.5, p. 431 (2017: Definition 9.13, p. 317)
book.statement: $K \subseteq M_i$ has measure zero if for every smooth chart $\varphi$ of $M_i$ the set $\varphi(U \cap K)$ has Lebesgue measure zero.

lean.statement: $K \subseteq M$ has measure zero if its image in every chart has Lebesgue measure zero; measure zero is monotone and closed under countable unions, can be checked on a cover by charts, and $\mathbb R^2$ itself does not have it.

diff: For Mathlib manifolds with corners (Findings, Chapter 9, item 70).

items.title: Lemma 9.4.6 (2017: 9.14), non-essential points form a null set

book.label: §9.4, Lemma 9.4.6, p. 431 (2017: Lemma 9.14, p. 317)
book.statement: The sets $K(i, i')^{ne}$ have measure zero (by a Lebesgue density argument).

lean.statement: For every subset $K$ of a finite-dimensional manifold, $K \setminus K^e$ has measure zero, by a Lebesgue density argument at points where the relative tangent space is not everything.

diff: Any $K$, not only $K(i, i')$; for M-polyfold sheets it is the field `isNull_diff_ess` of `SheetGeometry` (gap G.105) (Findings, Chapter 9, items 70, 72).

items.title: Definition 9.4.7 (2017: 9.14), $y$-equivalence

book.label: §9.4, Definition 9.4.7, p. 432 (2017: Definition 9.14, p. 318)
book.statement: $i \sim_y i'$ if there is a chain $i = i_0, \ldots, i_k = i'$ in $I_y$ with $y \in K(i_{p-1}, i_p)^e$; then $T_yM_i = T_yM_{i'}$; $P_y = I_y/{\sim_y}$.

book.statement: The set $\{y \in M_U \mid \#(I_y/{\sim_y}) \ge 2\}$ has measure zero.

items.title: Proposition 9.4.9 (2017: 9.5), the decomposition of $M^*_U$

book.label: §9.4, Proposition 9.4.9, p. 434 (2017: Proposition 9.5, p. 319)
book.statement: $M^*_U = \{y \in M_U \mid \#P_y = 1\}$ differs from $M_U$ by a null set and is the disjoint union of the $M^J_U = \{y \in M^*_U \mid I_y = J\}$; on $M^J_U$: (1) $\Theta = \sigma_J$, (2) $T_\Theta = \sigma_J T^J_y$, (3) $\hat T_\Theta = a_J (T^J_y, o^a_J) + b_J (T^J_y, o^b_J)$, (4) $a_J + b_J = \sigma_J$, $o^a_J = -o^b_J$.

The footnote's "Lemma 9.5.2" is a forward reference (Findings, Chapter 9, items 72, 74).

items.title: Proposition 9.4.10 (2017: 9.6), comparing two oriented structures
